EMI / PI Safeguarding Assessment (/arckit:uk-fs-safeguarding)

The /arckit:uk-fs-safeguarding command generates a safeguarding assessment for an authorised UK Electronic Money Institution (EMI) or Authorised Payment Institution (API) under the Electronic Money Regulations 2011…

Back to Guides

A short AI-narrated film with English captions. Pressing play loads the YouTube player. Watch on YouTube

Status: EXPERIMENTAL · Community-contributed · CRITICAL SEVERITY · Output is not regulatory advice. Safeguarding failures have led to firm collapse and FCA enforcement action. The safeguarding assessment MUST be reviewed, materially supplemented, and signed off by qualified UK FS regulatory counsel, the director or senior manager responsible for safeguarding oversight (CASS 15.2.4R; an SMF holder only if the firm is within SM&CR), the firm's MLRO (for AML-angle review of the client-money position), and the firm's Compliance Officer before any production safeguarding arrangement is established. Verify the FCA Approach Document (current edition), PS25/12 (August 2025) and the CASS 15 rules in force from 7 May 2026 for changes introduced since this command was authored.

Purpose

The /arckit:uk-fs-safeguarding command generates a safeguarding assessment for an authorised UK Electronic Money Institution (EMI) or Authorised Payment Institution (API) under the Electronic Money Regulations 2011 (EMR 2011 Reg 20–22), the Payment Services Regulations 2017 (PSRs 2017 Reg 23) and, from 7 May 2026, the FCA's CASS 15 rules (FCA 2025/38, made under PS25/12). It also covers Small Payment Institutions (SPIs) that elect to safeguard voluntarily (PSRs 2017 Reg 23(16)–(17)).

The artefact documents the firm's chosen safeguarding method, the designated safeguarding bank or insurer arrangements, the end-to-end client-funds flow, the daily reconciliation framework, and an audit plan aligned to FCA supervisory expectations including the monthly safeguarding return (REP027: SUP 16.14A, content in SUP 16 Annex 29BR; one return for PIs and EMIs).

Safeguarding is a continuous operational obligation — not a one-time setup task. This document must be reviewed at least annually and whenever the firm's products, volumes, or safeguarding bank arrangements change.

When to Use

  • Before launching a client-funds product — any EMI or API product where the firm holds relevant funds (as defined in PSRs 2017 Reg 2 / EMR 2011 Reg 2) on behalf of customers requires a documented safeguarding arrangement before those funds are received.
  • After a safeguarding bank change — if the firm switches or adds a designated safeguarding bank account or insurer, the assessment must be updated and re-signed by the individual responsible for safeguarding oversight.
  • PS25/12 compliance refresh — the FCA's PS25/12 (August 2025) made the CASS 15 safeguarding rules, SUP 3A safeguarding audits and the monthly safeguarding return, in force 7 May 2026 (FCA 2025/38). If the firm's existing documentation was drafted before then, this command provides a structured refresh.
  • Pre-FCA supervisory engagement — before a skilled-person review (s166) or Dear CEO letter response, the firm needs current, traceable safeguarding documentation.
  • For SPI voluntary safeguarding — SPIs are not required to safeguard, but if an SPI elects to do so voluntarily, the same Reg 23 mechanics apply and the insolvency-priority protection under Reg 23(14)–(15) follows. This command covers that voluntary case explicitly.

Inputs

Pass the project ID and product context as $ARGUMENTS:

/arckit:uk-fs-safeguarding 002 B2B virtual-account product

The argument should include:

  • The project number or an existing project directory name.
  • A brief description of the product in scope (used to contextualise the method statement and client-funds flow diagram).
  • Optionally: the firm's authorisation type (EMI / API / SPI), the intended safeguarding method (segregation / insurance / guarantee), and the name of the designated safeguarding bank (if already chosen).

If this information is not in $ARGUMENTS, the command reads it from the project's REQ and DATA artefacts where present, and prompts for it in the output summary where missing.

Output

Doc-type code: FSSAFE (CRITICAL severity)

Output path: projects/<NNN>-<slug>/payments-compliance/ARC-<NNN>-FSSAFE-v1.0.md

The generated artefact contains the following sections:

  1. Document Control (classification, owner, safeguarding oversight under CASS 15.2.4R, review cycle)
  2. Firm Authorisation Profile (authorisation type, FCA FRN, whether the firm is within SM&CR, products in scope)
  3. Safeguarding Method Statement (chosen method with explicit regulatory justification)
  4. Designated Safeguarding Arrangements (bank account details / insurer / guarantor)
  5. End-to-end Client Funds Flow (Mermaid or ASCII diagram + narrative for each node)
  6. Reconciliation Framework (daily cadence, four-tier sign-off chain, variance handling)
  7. Audit Plan (internal audit cadence, external auditor role under SUP 3A, monthly safeguarding return evidence pack)
  8. Failure Scenarios and Recovery (safeguarding bank failure, reconciliation shortfall, payout blockage — at minimum three scenarios)
  9. References (all required citations)

Key Regulatory Anchors

Three safeguarding methods are available:

Method Regulatory basis Requirements
Segregation in designated account EMR 2011 Reg 21; PSRs 2017 Reg 23(5)–(11) Funds kept segregated from receipt; if still held at the end of the business day following the day of receipt, placed in a separate designated account or invested in relevant assets (PSRs 2017 Reg 23(5)–(6); EMR 2011 Reg 21(1)–(2)); for EMIs, funds received by payment instrument safeguarded by the end of five business days after the e-money is issued (EMR 2011 Reg 20(4)); no commingling with operational funds
Comparable insurance policy EMR 2011 Reg 22; PSRs 2017 Reg 23(12)–(13) Relevant funds must be covered, so the policy must be in place BEFORE they are received; proceeds payable into a designated account on insolvency; notify the FCA at least 2 months before first reliance (CASS 15.5.7R)
Comparable guarantee EMR 2011 Reg 22; PSRs 2017 Reg 23(12)–(13) Guarantee must be in place BEFORE relevant funds are received; same CASS 15.5.7R notification

Monthly safeguarding return: REP027, submitted within 15 business days of each month end (SUP 16.14A.3R), with its content set by SUP 16 Annex 29BR. One return covers authorised PIs, authorised and small EMIs, credit unions issuing e-money and SPIs that opt in (FCA Approach Document, May 2026, Chapter 13). The FCA Handbook is a single-page application: open SUP 16 at https://handbook.fca.org.uk/handbook/sup16 and find SUP 16.14A and Annex 29BR in the chapter.

FCA enforcement context: Two firm failures show why safeguarding is CRITICAL severity:

  • Allied Wallet (2019–2020): an EMI. On 4 June 2019 the FCA imposed requirements stopping it carrying on regulated activities or disposing of the funds it held, then petitioned to wind it up because it appeared to be mixing funds received from merchants and card issuers with its own. The High Court made a winding-up order on 20 March 2020 and later found the FCA's concern well-founded, with significant sums missing (FCA statement; Re Allied Wallet Ltd [2022] EWHC 1877 (Ch), judgment).
  • Premier FX (collapsed 2018; censured 2021): an API providing money remittance. After its sole director died in June 2018 it could not meet customers' claims, and administrators were appointed on the FCA's application on 13 August 2018. The FCA's Final Notice of 23 February 2021 publicly censured it for safeguarding and payment-account breaches between 2013 and 2018: only its main sterling account was designated as a client account, and customer funds were commingled with other customers' and the firm's own funds (Final Notice). Customers with accepted claims were repaid in full after Barclays, the firm's bank, made a voluntary payment of £10,076,943.75 (FCA, 18 December 2023).

Both cases show that safeguarding is not a one-time setup: segregation, account designation and ongoing reconciliation are the controls that failed in practice.

PS25/12 (FCA, August 2025) made the Payments and Electronic Money (Safeguarding) Instrument 2025 (FCA 2025/38), in force 7 May 2026: CASS 15 (relevant funds), CASS 10A (resolution pack), SUP 3A (safeguarding audits) and SUP 16.14A (monthly safeguarding return). CP24/20 (September 2024) was the consultation that preceded it. The FCA Approach Document (May 2026 edition, Chapters 10 and 13) is the current primary reference for FCA supervisory expectations.

Composes With

Command Relationship
/arckit:uk-fs-ctp-dependency The safeguarding bank or insurer is itself a critical third-party dependency. The CTP dependency register should include the safeguarding bank as a candidate designated or material non-CTP.
/arckit:risk Safeguarding failure is a high-impact Orange Book risk. Cross-reference it in the project risk register with the FSSAFE document ID.
/arckit:operationalize The reconciliation runbook is a day-2 operational artefact. Once the safeguarding assessment defines the reconciliation cadence and sign-off chain, assemble the operational runbook via /arckit:operationalize.
/arckit:adr The safeguarding method choice (segregation vs insurance vs guarantee) is an architectural decision with cost, operational, and regulatory implications — record it as an ADR for traceability.

Important Caveats

  • Safeguarding obligations apply from the moment funds are received, not when payment is initiated. The segregation trigger is receipt of funds. Any float period between receipt and placement in the designated account must be explicitly documented, minimised, and approved by the individual responsible for safeguarding oversight.
  • Insurance and guarantee methods require the policy to be in place BEFORE the relevant funds are received. EMR 2011 Reg 22(1) and PSRs 2017 Reg 23(12) require the funds to be covered, so a retroactive arrangement does not satisfy them. From 7 May 2026 the firm must also notify the FCA at least 2 months before first relying on the method or changing the cover or the provider (CASS 15.5.7R).
  • Reconcile at least once each reconciliation day. CASS 15.8.19R (internal) and CASS 15.8.42R (external) require safeguarding reconciliations as frequently as necessary and no less than once each reconciliation day (a business day), from 7 May 2026. Intraday reconciliation is the firm's own decision based on its volumes; there is no regulatory volume threshold for it.
  • Define the FCA notification triggers for shortfalls explicitly. CASS 15.8.60R requires the firm to inform the FCA in writing without delay in the cases it lists, including a material failure to reconcile or to pay a shortfall into a relevant funds account. "Materially" has no numeric threshold: the firm must document its own (e.g., a shortfall exceeding £X or Y% of safeguarded funds), have it approved by the Compliance Officer, and ensure it triggers notification to the individual responsible for safeguarding oversight and the FCA.
  • Name the individual responsible for safeguarding oversight; do not assume SM&CR. CASS 15.2.4R requires every safeguarding institution to allocate to a single director or senior manager responsibility for overseeing operational compliance with the relevant funds regime and reporting on it to the governing body. SM&CR applies only to FSMA-authorised firms (those with a Part 4A permission, such as a bank or building society). A PI or EMI authorised only under the PSRs 2017 or EMRs 2011 is outside it: its directors and persons responsible for management are assessed for good repute and knowledge under PSRs 2017 regulation 6(7)(b) or EMRs 2011 regulation 6(6)(b) (the "PSD Individual" or "EMD Individual"; FCA Approach Document, May 2026, paragraphs 3.107 to 3.111). Use SMF titles only for a firm within SM&CR. HM Treasury's Modernising Payment Services Regulation consultation (14 July to 6 October 2026) asked whether senior managers of payment and e-money institutions should carry enhanced accountability; check whether a decision has followed.
  • The safeguarding bank is itself a critical dependency. If the safeguarding bank fails, freezes the account, or terminates the relationship, the firm may be unable to meet payout obligations within the regulatory timeframe. The CTP dependency register must include the safeguarding bank.
  • The monthly safeguarding return is SUP 16 Annex 29BR, not Annex 30A, 34A or 34B. SUP 16.14A requires the return and SUP 16 Annex 29BR sets its content; there is one return for PIs and EMIs. SUP 16 Annex 30 lists the e-money institution returns, and REP-CRIM is the Annual Financial Crime Report (SUP 16.23, SUP 16 Annex 42AR). Neither is the safeguarding return.
  • Design for the monthly safeguarding return before the system is built. Design the reconciliation data flow to produce the fields SUP 16 Annex 29BR asks for — retrofitting reporting fields after go-live is a common and costly error.
